title: Nessa and the Berry
markdown:
The Moonmallow Mountains were sleepy and quiet. The air felt soft, like a bedtime story spoken low. Ferny silver-birches glowed a little. The moon, round and white as a marshmallow, peeked over the peaks. Moonbeams lay on the path. Leaves moved like tiny dancers.

Nessa Pine was a young ogre who did not stomp or roar. Her feet tiptoed on moss. Her big hands stayed gentle. She listened to rustling leaves and sleepy birds tucking in. Trees nodded, branches like friendly arms. Her heart was as soft as the moss. Her eyes were curious as a deer’s. Her tunic sparkled as if sewn from moonlight.

She walked around a twisty birch whose bark looked like a smiley face, and heard a sound: a soft rumbling grumble, a busy bee trying to lift a stone. Grumble-wumph. Grumble-wumph. Trying hard.

In the shadows by green moss, a little creature, round and fuzzy, feelers like silver threads tasting the night. It was pushing a berry.

The berry was as big as the creature’s head, plump, shiny with dew, a tiny sunset. The fuzzy thing pushed and wiggled and grumbled. The berry stayed put. The grumble said, I will move this berry.

Nessa’s chest felt warm. She smiled and tiptoed closer, boots silent. Soft green fur, a gentle firefly-glow that had decided to stay. Feelers pointed like little arrows. A Moon-Moth Grub, taking its berry home to a burrow under a moonpetal flower.

“Hello there,” Nessa whispered, dandelion-seed soft.

The grub stopped. It tilted its fuzzy head. Dewdrop eyes looked up. It did not seem scared. Nessa was only a gentle shadow, a still pond of an ogre.

She wondered if the berry had rolled from a bush that tickled clouds. The grub gave another push. Grumble-wumph. A tiny engine of trying.

“That looks very big,” she said, and reached, not to grab, to nudge, light as a falling feather.

The berry did not merely move. It rolled, whoosh, as if it had been waiting. It had not been stuck. It had been resting on a slick patch of moss, a tiny green slide. The grub wiggled its whole body, a happy buzzy wiggle. Glow flickered. Feelers danced.

A cheerful humming arrived, bees in sweet flowers. “Ooh, what a splendid berry!” A little goblin with rosy cheeks and a hat stuck with tiny berries skipped into view: Gribble the jam-maker, always hunting juice for Moonmallow Mountain Jam that tasted of sunshine and giggles. “And who is helping our little fuzzy friend?”

Nessa’s face lit. “I was just helping. The berry was on slippery moss.”

Gribble chuckled, little bells. “Dewy after sunset. Quite slippery.” From his pocket a tiny leaf cup, a small green boat. He poured a drop of spiderweb dew that sparkled like a diamond. “A treat for a busy helper. And for our kind ogre friend too.”

The grub sipped, sip-sip. The berry was not for jam today. It was for the determined little worker. After effort and dew, its glow held steady.

It nudged the berry, then looked up at Nessa. Feelers gave a thank-you wiggle. She knelt. Moss-green skin met the forest floor. A quiet fuzzy friend who loved big berries, sparkly dew, and gentle moonlight.

The grub settled beside its prize. Nessa sat too. Silver colours. Damp earth. Sweet moss. Gribble waved his berry-hat and hummed down the mountain, pleased. Nessa and the grub watched the marshmallow moon climb. Velvety sky. A cricket far away. Wind in the pines. She felt safe, and cozy, and ready for sweet dreams under the watching stars, the twist of the evening already simple: a berry that only needed a slide, and a grub that had been trying all along.
